angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 194,796 km at 124.84 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.0106 +/- 0.0564 mas (same row, RUWE 0.99): 124.84 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.28 +/- 0.02 solar radii from de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-332 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract): 194,796 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.27 +/- 0.01 solar masses from de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-332 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3315 +/- 137 K from de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-332 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: de Leon et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-332 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.508..195D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-332.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.975, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
